newsitem.title: USA: CME Jan lumber ends limit down for second day.
newsitem.headline: CME Jan lumber ends limit down for second day.

text.p: A late morning short-covering rally lacked follow through and January CME lumber futures again fell its $10.00-per-thousand-board-foot daily limit at the close, traders said.
Short covering boosted January to $383.00 per tbf after it opened limit down offered. Fund liquidation then knocked Jan down its limit after buying lacked follow through.

January ended limit down at $374.80 per tbf while other months finished $4.00 lower to $2.50 higher with only distant November up. March ended down $4.00 at $364.80. Trading limits will be $15.00 Thursday after the two limit closes.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $425 per tbf, down $48 from last Friday and $55 under the last midweek quote.

The sharp drop in cash spruce prices added to carryover sell stops to open January limit down. General short covering developed as prices appeared oversold, but the market turned weak again when talk circulated that cash prices were still falling, traders said.
"The (cash) market is in a freefall - the speculative bubble has finally burst and prices are coming back to earth pretty quick," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney forest products analyst.
Cash spruce prices will likely fall to $400 or less before stabilizing, cash sources said.

Declines in deferred contracts were held in check by their sharp discount to cash lumber prices, sources noted. For example, May 1997 lumber futures closed at $354.30 per tbf, down $2.20, well below Random Lengths quote for cash lumber at $425.00.
Also, despite some opinions to the contrary, some traders said cash markets are expected to recover somewhat after the current break is completed.
